carnage.name: Jakobm90
carnage.commentary: That’s a full-course detour into the weeds. One hole turned into a 10 because the round already had enough trouble without giving the scoreboard a fattened-up disaster entrée.

carnage.name: derekldavis
carnage.commentary: Same old rude reminder: one par 5 swallowed him whole and spit out a 10. When the worst hole is that loud, the rest of the card is basically just damage control with a scorecard.

carnage.name: Leroy4522
carnage.commentary: A par 5 nine is the kind of hole that says ‘thanks for coming’ and locks the door behind you. Not exactly the sort of momentum builder you want when the putter is already acting allergic to birdies.

players.name: derekldavis
players.tagline: His putter showed up with a knife and his tee ball mailed in the rest.
players.body: This was another grim but familiar net survival act: he stayed in the fight on the leaderboard, but the golf underneath was all kinds of busted. The ball was at least mostly in play, yet the round got kneecapped by too many doubles and a brutal stretch on the greens, where the putter basically went on strike and collected three three-putts for its trouble. The worst hole was the kind that ruins your mood and your lunch, a par 5 turned into a 10, and the late-round damage never really got patched up. Four starts in, the profile is pretty clear: he can keep the wheels from fully falling off, but the ceiling is still being dragged down by the big numbers and a putter that keeps acting like it’s unionized against him.

players.name: Leroy4522
players.tagline: The driver wandered off and the short game didn’t file a missing-person report.
players.body: This was a messy, sideways round that finished better than it looked and looked worse than it should have. He still found enough fairways to keep the card from going completely feral, but the approach play and short game did the heavy lifting for the wrong reasons, leaving too many ugly looks and not enough bailout options. The longest ball of the day wasn’t the problem; the problem was that the rest of the bag refused to capitalize, and the round never found a birdie to soften the bruise. The par 5 nine on the worst hole was the headline crime scene. After 13 starts, the broader picture is still mixed: he’s good enough to avoid total collapse, but the scoring punch is too thin and the bogeys keep showing up like unpaid bills.

players.name: Jakobm90
players.tagline: The big stick finally RSVP’d, then the irons crashed the party.
players.body: This was the weird kind of round where the tee ball showed up looking dangerous, but the rest of the bag kept tripping over its own shoelaces. He absolutely nuked it off the tee at times and still managed to pile up better-than-average fairway work, yet the approach game was the real anchor, leaving way too many ugly second shots and a bunch of damage that the putter couldn’t fully erase. The headline hole was the 13th, where a par 4 turned into a 10 and basically torched the card’s good behavior. With four prior starts, the trend is getting harder to ignore: the ceiling is real when the driver cooperates, but the iron play is volatile enough to keep turning promising golf into a ransom note.
